subject: alchemistWorkbench
pitch:
Category: Prop group.
Subject: alchemist's workbench with potions, books, scales and herbs.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
This fits best as a prop group since it's a scenery piece without joints — a workbench with potions, books, scales, and herbs arranged on it. I'm leaning toward a cel-shaded anime aesthetic with glowing potion effects and bold, clean color blocks to capture that Genshin Impact feel, likely drawing on toon shading and glow kits.

I want to plan the module structure carefully — using the builder from the SDK, setting up the right exports, and figuring out an appropriate scope given it's a prop group rather than a full rigged character. I'm thinking somewhere in the range of several hundred lines to properly flesh out the table, items, and shading details, while double-checking the correct API calls since I won't be able to test-run this.

I'll create a single "bench" joint at the origin to satisfy the root requirement, then build parts off it using `b.part` with position, direction, and axis options for orientation. I'm noting the other builder helpers available—sweep, rod, capsule, spike, frustumBox—and especially `b.lathe` for rotationally symmetric shapes like potion flasks and vials, where the outline points define the profile from the axis outward and back.

I'm sketching a lathe outline for a flask shape, then considering extrude for flat objects like books, and cataloging more builder methods: stick, surface, decal, and especially cards for creating herb leaves from textured sprites on sprigs.

For the Genshin-style aesthetic I'm planning cel shading throughout with the toon kit, pairing it with grain paints for wood textures like a workbench tabletop, and reminding myself to skip adding ground or scenery props unless the brief explicitly calls for them.

I'm sketching the actual scene now: a 1.6m-wide wooden alchemy workbench around 0.9m tall, holding glowing potion flasks, stacked books, brass scales, and maybe hanging herb bundles from a rail above, all rendered in warm amber wood tones against jade and gold accents with vivid potion colors glowing via the glow kit.

Working out the bench geometry with turned, baluster-style legs via lathe profiles for that stylized Genshin furniture look, plus a chunky slab top and lower stretcher rails for support.

I'm now planning the texture set needed for decoration: an emblem sigil for the apron front, label and parchment textures for potion bottles and books, leather cover textures with gold tooling, and herb/leaf card textures — aiming for roughly 5-12 distinct textures total to give the scene variety.

For the books, I'm thinking closed books as boxes with cover paint and a top-face decal for the cover design, plus an open book made from two angled page planes forming a V shape, built from thin boxes rotated into position with page-line textures.

For potions, I'm planning round-bottom flask shapes using lathe geometry with colored liquid inside.

Without transparency, nesting the liquid lathe inside the glass would just hide it, so I'll rethink the structure—make the glass a thin ring at the neck and base, letting the liquid itself form the visible bulb surface instead.

Simplifying further, I'll just make the glass a single stylized solid lathe shape for the bottle body, and keep the liquid as a separate glowing lathe nested just inside it rather than trying to model true transparency.

I'm planning to add a small white sphere stuck to the surface as a highlight bubble, plus tiny glowing spheres for sparkle accents. For variety I'm sketching out potion types — magenta round flask, cyan tall vial with cork, green squat jar, gold crystal bottle — each distinguished by shape, glow color, and a front-facing label plane with texture, positioned slightly offset from the surface.

Now I'm working out how to apply the labels as decals that conform to the bottle's curved surface, using a surface-hit point and direction to project the texture onto the glass without needing glow on the paper itself. Then I shift to designing the brass balance scale: a base cylinder, a central post, a horizontal beam rod with a pivot knob, and two shallow lathe-dish pans hanging from chains.

I'm planning the pans' suspension points on the beam tips, connecting them to the pan rims with thin chain rods, then moving on to hanging herb bundles from a wooden rail above the bench and adding a mortar and pestle for alchemical flavor. I'm also weighing whether to add a small back shelf with jars and books to give the bench more height and visual interest, while keeping the prop count restrained.

Since the back shelving counts as part of the workbench the brief already names, I'll keep it simple with two uprights and a rail rather than a full structure, and I'm staying mindful of part and triangle budgets so things stay performant. For the Genshin-style look I'm thinking through cel shading, ink outline lines on creases, and gold trim details, along with wood grain paint textures running along the boards and warm amber color choices for the bench surfaces.

Potion liquids need saturated Genshin-like colors like magenta, cyan, gold, green, and violet, kept as flat colors rather than painted textures so the glow effect (which drives emissive) works correctly — I'm checking the type signatures to confirm glow accepts the lathe-generated Part structure properly.

I'm now planning the SVG decal textures, like an apron emblem with a flask and star sigil in gold, and figuring out how to mount it as a plane geometry positioned just in front of the apron surface using the right orientation and axis settings.

I'm also sketching out label textures for potion bottles — a round flask label with a rune and a strip-style vial label with stars — plus a leather book cover texture with gold tooling lines applied as a transparent overlay plane, and starting to think through a page texture next.

Settling on roughly seven textures total: emblem, label, cover tooling, page, leaf, sprig, and star. For hanging herb bundles, I'm thinking of sweeping stem paths downward from the rail and scattering leaf cards along the bottom using frames collected from `b.along`, which places oriented points along a path that I can feed into the card-placement function.

For hanging leaves I'm thinking through how lean and flow interact with the tangent direction on the stem, trying to get leaves to splay outward radially rather than facing straight down. I'll use a flow function per card that computes a radial direction based on angle, flattened onto the plane perpendicular to the stem axis, to get the sideways hanging effect.

I'm also sorting out that `rng(seed)` returns a number generator function for variety in placement, and sketching how a hanging bundle works: a tie point on the rail, rod sweeps running down to spread tip points, then cards placed along each rod using `b.along`.

For the sprig helper, I'm planning a function taking start/end points, leaf texture, color, and seed, using simple `[x,y,z]` tuples for points passed into `b.rod`.
